messages.subject: [statnet_help] Understanding dyad in statnet
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

According to the term dyadcov in statnet library:

With the parameter of ?dyadcov? term, we add three statistics to the model,
each equal to the sum of the covariate values for all dyads occupying one
of the three possible non-empty dyad states (mutual, upper-triangular
asymmetric, and lower-triangular asymmetric dyads, respectively).

what is the difference between upper-triangular asymmetric dyads (utri) and
lower-triangular asymmetric dyads (ltri)?
Based on my understanding, it?s related to the direction of ties, see the
figure below. Is it right?

[image: Inline image 1]


Many thanks.

Best regards.

Chengjun Wang

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Re: bi-partite network with attributes, and run ergm
messages.body_plain:
Dear User community,

1) I have a bi-partite network data, and I have 159 nodes (b1), and 116 events (b2).  I have made my network into bi-partite in the below command. 

 I load my first mode (b1) attributes (its name="ethnicity3"), and run ergm model.  When I load my second mode (b2=events), I did NOT have any error message in R.  But, I tried to run ergm model with "b2factor" command with attribute name ("dom"), R shows error message, telling there is no such attributes name in vertex.

I look foward to your reply.

##read my edgelist
mydata<-read.table("edge.txt", stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

## transform event numbers which is consecutive from nodes, we have 159 nodes. 
mydata[, 2]<-mydata[, 2]+159

##change data from dataframe to network, 
##and set as bipartite w 159 nodes, undirected graph
netmydata<-network(mydata, bipartite=159, directed=F)

## read node attr list
nodeatt<-read.csv("node.csv", stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

## read event attr list
eventatt<-read.csv("event.csv", stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

## set 1st node attribute from 1:159
##var names:ethnicity3
set.vertex.attribute(netmydata, attrname=names(nodeatt)[1], value=nodeatt[, 1], v=1:159)

##set 1st event attribute from 160:275
set.vertex.attribute(netmydata, attrname=names(eventatt)[1], value=eventatt[, 1], v=160:275)
##var names:dom

##The following b1factor model can be run
resultb1<-ergm(netmydata~edges+b1factor("ethnicity3", base=1)+gwb1degree(0.25, fixed=T)+gwb2degree(0.25, fixed=T), seed=100)

##b2factor model can never run
resultb2<-ergm(netmydata~edges+b2factor("dom", base=1)+gwb1degree(0.25, fixed=T)+gwb2degree(0.25, fixed=T), seed=100)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

If I estimate a STERGM using CMLE with (time-varying) node attributes as 
covariates (say, as nodeicov), how do I have to interpret the nodal 
covariates? Let's say I have two time slices and a quantitative node 
attribute, which can change over time. Does it make sense to include 
both (1) the absolute attribute value of alter and (2) the change 
between the two time periods to predict tie formation and dissolution? 
Which of the two attribute vectors does STERGM use as a covariate -- the 
one at t=1 or the one at t=2 or some kind of pooled value or the 
absolute change between them?

Philip

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Preview release for Statnet suite packages (ergm, latentnet, and others).
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Preview release for Statnet suite packages (ergm, latentnet, and others).
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet Users,

Since our last release in March, we have fixed a number of bugs and made
a number of improvements to Statnet Project packages. This includes
valued ERGM functionality --- ERGMs for networks whose ties have
weights.

We have created a repository for a preview release (3.0-999) while the
packages make their way through the CRAN system. Installation
instructions can be found at: http://statnet.org/preview . The package
dependencies should install automatically if you follow these
instructions.

Both ergm and latentnet have been updated, and there are three new
packages:

       * tergm:  dynamic network modeling facilities (e.g.,
         stergm()); these were briefly a part of the ergm package,
         but have now been split out into their own R package.

       * ergm.count: extensions for fitting ERGMs to networks
         whose tie values are counts. (See Krivitsky (2012) reference in
         the package documentation for more information.)

       * statnet.common: A library with a set of routines used by other
         packages; it will install automatically

The preview packages have been tested internally, but they have not been
checked by CRAN and may be incomplete in other ways. We would very much
appreciate any bug reports and other feedback.

                             Pavel Krivitsky (for the Statnet Dev. Team)

messages.subject: [statnet_help] weighted network analysis with statnet ?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chengjun Wang,

> I am wondering whether statnet could deal with weighted network or
> not. Does anyone know?

The current version of network can handle them, and latentnet can fit
some models to them. There is a preview release of ergm
( http://www.statnet.org/preview ) which can fit ERGMs to counts of
interactions.

> I have tried to convert weighted network into adjacency matrix, does
> it work?
> 
> 
>         # get adjacency matrix
>          library(igraph)
>         gflow <- graph.data.frame(flows[,1:3], directed=T)
>         gflowWeight<-get.adjacency(gflow, type="both",
>         attr="clickstream")  
>         # get statnet object
>         library(statnet)
>         n=network(gflowWeight,vertex.attr=NULL,
>         vertex.attrnames=NULL,matrix.type="adjacency",directed=TRUE) #
>         creates an edgelist using the unique IDs

Try

n=as.network(gflowWeight,matrix.type="adjacency",directed=TRUE,names.eval="clickstream",ignore.eval=FALSE)

                               I hope this helps,
                               Pavel Krivitsky

messages.subject: [statnet_help] STERGM with time-varying nodal covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Philip,

> If I estimate a STERGM using CMLE with (time-varying) node attributes as 
> covariates (say, as nodeicov), how do I have to interpret the nodal 
> covariates? Let's say I have two time slices and a quantitative node 
> attribute, which can change over time. Does it make sense to include 
> both (1) the absolute attribute value of alter and (2) the change 
> between the two time periods to predict tie formation and dissolution? 

The two are distinct, though (2) might be difficult to interpret, unless
it can be assumed to be entirely exogenous to the network process. If it
is exogenous, its effect can be interpreted as the effect of that
particular attribute changing. (If it's not exogenous --- the state of
the network can affect it --- then it's not clear.)

> Which of the two attribute vectors does STERGM use as a covariate -- the 
> one at t=1 or the one at t=2 or some kind of pooled value or the 
> absolute change between them?

t=1 network's attributes are used to predict the transition.

                 I hope this helps,
                 Pavel
